Chip stocks dump again Summary: RBA Governor Bullock said inflation risks remain skewed to the upside, and the minutes showed six of nine members judged 4.85% “not clearly sufficient”. Three warned of a sharper downturn. New Zealand one-year inflation expectations jumped to 2.92%, while the two-year gauge held near 2.36%. Respondents see the OCR at 3.05% by year-end. Former BOJ chief Kuroda said rates may need to rise above neutral. Japan postponed its planned two-year floating-rate bond. Brent eased to around $91.80 on surplus expectations despite a tanker attack near Hormuz and Iranian claims of four strikes. Gold steadied near $3,868 after Monday’s one-year low. The Nikkei fell about 0.9%, the Kospi about 1.8% and Samsung more than 3% after the US imposed chip export licensing on five countries. The Reserve Bank of Australia set the tone in Asia on Tuesday. Governor Michele Bullock said inflation risks remain skewed to the upside, and minutes of the November meeting showed most board members judged the 4.85% cash rate “not clearly sufficient” to bring inflation back to target. Regional stocks fell as US chip export curbs weighed on technology names. Oil eased on expectations of a supply surplus, despite a fresh tanker attack near the Strait of Hormuz. Levels below are as of around 04:35 GMT. Central banks The RBA minutes revealed a divided board behind November’s hike. Six members cited rising inflation pressures, strong services inflation and a likely higher neutral rate. Three dissenters warned the economy might be nearing a materially sharper downturn. The board gave no explicit guidance. The minutes also noted that the forecasts assume oil prices fall by around US$30 a barrel over two years, leaving significant upside risk if prices stay high. AUD/USD held near 0.6740. In New Zealand, the RBNZ’s Survey of Expectations showed one-year inflation expectations jumping to 2.92% from 2.60%, while the closely watched two-year measure edged up only to 2.36%. Respondents expect the official cash rate to rise to 3.05% by year-end from 2.75%, ahead of the 9 December Monetary Policy Statement. NZD/USD was little changed near 0.5495. In Japan, former BOJ Governor Haruhiko Kuroda said rates may need to rise above neutral if inflation worsens, citing cost pressures from the Iran war. He also called the government’s planned food sales tax cut inflationary. Separately, the Finance Ministry postponed its planned two-year floating-rate government bond, according to sources, because markets already price in BOJ hikes. USD/JPY eased to around 159.20, and the 10-year JGB yield was near 2.89%. Oil and geopolitics Brent slipped to around $91.80 a barrel as an International Energy Agency forecast of a fourth-quarter supply surplus outweighed renewed attacks on shipping. A tanker transiting Hormuz was disabled near Khasab, Oman, according to UK maritime authorities, and Iran’s navy claimed four tanker strikes in 24 hours. The US Army is seeking to build 17 concrete bunkers at bases in Israel, Saudi Arabia and Lebanon. CNN reported US intelligence on Iranian contingency planning for an attack in Washington, which officials said was not imminent. The surplus narrative is driving prices for now, but such explanations tend to follow price and can change quickly. Gold Gold steadied near $3,868 an ounce, up around 0.3%, after touching a one-year low near $3,830 on Monday as Treasury yields above 5% and a firm dollar weighed. Bank views remain sharply divided. Morgan Stanley named gold its top commodity pick, with a $5,250 target for late 2027, while Goldman Sachs sees $4,650. Silver rose about 1%. Equities Asian stocks fell after the US required licenses for advanced chip exports to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil, aiming to curb Chinese access to AI computing: The Nikkei 225 lost about 0.9% to around 59,100, and the Topix fell around 1.7%. The Kospi dropped roughly 1.8%, with Samsung Electronics down more than 3%. The Hang Seng slipped about 0.8%, and the Shanghai Composite was flat. US futures were mixed: S&P 500 futures were little changed and Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 0.3%. Bitcoin held near $64,950. Bank views Goldman Sachs Asset Management expects Fed hikes in both December and January after a third firm reading on core inflation. PIMCO urged investors to lock in bond yields near 25-year highs. Morgan Stanley set an 8,700 S&P 500 target for end-2027. Goldman Sachs forecast a 24% return for the Topix over the next 12 months, saying Japan’s rally may broaden to more sectors. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.content: Mark43 Sets the Standard for Responsible AI in Public Safety with Report AI and BriefAI Mark43 Sets the Standard for Responsible AI in Public Safety with Report AI and BriefAI Built directly into the workflows and data agencies already use, these AI capabilities reduce administrative burden, improve report quality, and accelerate investigations the leading cloud-native public safety operations platform, announced the general availability of Mark43 ReportAI and Mark43 BriefAI. Built directly into the workflows and data agencies already use, these AI capabilities reduce administrative burden, improve report quality, and accelerate investigations. Piloted with agencies including the Louisville Metropolitan Police Department, both tools are now available to all Mark43 customers across its integrated Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) and Records Management System (RMS) platform. The launch sets a new standard for AI in public safety. It is embedded within a responsible framework grounded in human oversight, security and compliance, and full transparency, agencies remain in control of when and how AI is used. “Public safety agencies need AI that seamlessly works inside the tools they already use every day,” said . “That’s exactly what ReportAI and BriefAI deliver. AI built into the platform, not bolted on, with the security and accountability that public safety demands. What used to take hours now takes minutes, giving officers time back, helping investigators move faster, and keeping the focus where it belongs: on the community.” Agencies today face growing case complexity, rising documentation standards, and persistent staffing shortages. Nearly 70% of U.S. agencies report officer shortages and 78% struggle to recruit qualified candidates. Every hour spent on paperwork is time off the street, and that gap is widening. Most AI solutions ask agencies to change how they work. Mark43 does not. ReportAI and BriefAI are embedded directly into existing workflows, connected to their CAD and RMS data, body-worn camera transcripts, and with the security, transparency, and human oversight that public safety requires. Robin Oates, Director of the Records Management Division at the Louisville Metropolitan Police Department , shared “Our officers are expected to apply complex policies and nuanced NIBRS rules while documenting fast-moving incidents. With AI-powered validations acting as a copilot, we can guide officers in real time, helping them meet reporting standards, capture the right details, and stay aligned with policy without relying solely on supervisor review. This reduces preventable errors, improves consistency and completeness, and allows our Records team and supervisors to focus on higher-value review instead of catching routine issues.” ReportAI: Faster, More Accurate Reports from the Scene ReportAI enables patrol officers to complete accurate, policy-compliant reports in the field, often before they leave the scene. Drawing on CAD data, body-worn camera transcripts, officer notes, and full event context, it generates comprehensive first drafts in seconds. Narratives are auto-generated, structured fields are pre-populated, and repetitive data entry is eliminated. Built-in validations check for completeness, narrative quality, and policy compliance before submission, catching issues early, reducing downstream corrections, and improving supervisor review. Officers remain in control at every step through role-based permissions and oversight. BriefAI: Case Intelligence for Investigators and Command Staff BriefAI gives supervisors, investigators, and command staff instant visibility into case scope and complexity. It generates concise, standardized summaries capturing who, what, when and where, and what needs to happen next. articles.title: Five hustles that can grow KSh 10,000 to KSh 100,000 in 30 days in Nairobi
articles.desc: From mitumba trading to freelancing, Nairobi’s streets and digital platforms are offering young entrepreneurs a credible shot at rapid returns on modest capital. By Yvonne Wambui Five small businesses available to Nairobi entrepreneurs with as little as KSh 10,000 have been identified as holding gen
articles.content: From mitumba trading to freelancing, Nairobi’s streets and digital platforms are offering young entrepreneurs a credible shot at rapid returns on modest capital. By Yvonne Wambui Five small businesses available to Nairobi entrepreneurs with as little as KSh 10,000 have been identified as holding genuine potential to grow that capital tenfold within 30 days — provided they are managed with discipline, strategy and consistent reinvestment. As the cost of living rises and formal employment remains out of reach for many young Kenyans, side hustles and small enterprises have moved from fallback option to primary income source for a growing number of people. The five opportunities outlined here span physical trade, food vending, digital commerce and skills-based work — meaning there is a viable entry point regardless of background or prior experience. Mitumba selling tops the list and remains one of the most accessible businesses in the city. Traders source second-hand clothing from markets such as Gikomba and River Road at low wholesale prices and resell at a margin through physical stalls or, increasingly, via WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram. The shift to social media has removed the barrier of shop rental, allowing sellers to reach customers across Nairobi and beyond from a smartphone. Street food vending is the second opportunity and one of the most immediately profitable for those willing to put in the hours. Selling smokies, boiled eggs and affordable snacks at bus stops, construction sites, universities and busy office areas requires minimal capital and can generate consistent daily income. The formula is straightforward: good hygiene, competitive pricing and a high-footfall location. Get those three right and a street food business can scale quickly. Fresh juice and fruit vending is the third hustle and a natural fit for Nairobi’s urban pace. Entrepreneurs buy watermelons, mangoes and pineapples in bulk from wholesale markets and convert them into fresh juice or ready-to-eat portions for commuters and office workers seeking affordable refreshments. Demand is strong, margins are reasonable and the business can be operated from a single cart or table. Freelancing is the fourth option and the most skills-dependent on the list. Young people with abilities in writing, graphic design, social media management or virtual assistance can market their services through LinkedIn, Twitter and local Facebook groups to build a client base without any physical stock or premises. The barrier to entry is internet access and the confidence to pitch — both increasingly within reach for Nairobi’s youth. Online selling through dropshipping and social commerce rounds out the five. This model allows entrepreneurs to market clothing, shoes, beauty products and household accessories through WhatsApp Business and Facebook without holding significant inventory, arranging delivery only once a sale is confirmed. It is lean, low-risk and scalable. A word of honest caution: turning KSh 10,000 into KSh 100,000 in a single month is not guaranteed and requires genuine commitment, smart reinvestment and an understanding of customers’ needs. Those operating physical businesses must also comply with Nairobi County licensing requirements, and food handlers are expected to meet public health standards. Success in any of these ventures is determined not by the size of the starting capital, but by the quality of the decisions made with it. articles.title: With the recruitment platform Research For Me closed since March, UNC researchers struggle to find study participants
articles.desc: The platform connects community members, patients and students with active research studies at UNC and across North Carolina.
articles.content: With the recruitment platform Research For Me closed since March, UNC researchers struggle to find study participants – The Daily Tar Heel With the recruitment platform Research For Me closed since March, UNC researchers struggle to find study participants The platform connects community members, patients and students with active research studies at UNC and across North Carolina. After being unable to list new studies for nearly eight months, UNC’s Research For Me recruitment platform is expected to return by the end of 2026, according to Laura Viera, assistant vice chancellor for clinical research. Research For Me is an online database and recruitment platform created through the University’s North Carolina Translational and Clinical Sciences Institute. The website connects community members, patients and students with active research studies at UNC and across the state. Following its launch in November 2019, Research For Me quickly became a key recruitment tool for researchers. Within two years, nearly 15,000 users had registered on the website, which had attracted more than 40,000 unique visitors, according to UNC Health. However, in March, users discovered that the website was no longer presenting new study listings. A system notice on the website read: “Due to technical difficulties, the full website has not been restored. This is a temporary solution to allow continued access to research study information while a complete resolution is being developed.” Keely Muscatell, an assistant professor in the Department of Psychology and Neuroscience who runs the Social Neuroscience and Health Lab, said she does not recall receiving a notification that Research For Me had become inaccessible. She also said she never received an explanation of the suspension or when researchers might regain access. “It came as a real surprise, and honestly, just a big disappointment in terms of, I thought it was a great service that the University could provide, especially when we think about expanding participation in research,” Muscatell said. The suspension followed the identification of a security vulnerability in REDCap — or Research Electronic Data Capture — a web-based application UNC and other universities use to support research studies and operations, Viera said. The vulnerability could have allowed an unauthorized person to gain remote access to the application, according to the University of Nebraska Medical Center. Upon discovering the issue, Viera said, UNC immediately took REDCap offline. According to Viera, UNC was able to restore REDCap’s other functions within UNC Research. However, issues with other software used to operate Research For Me could not be resolved, prompting the University to rebuild the platform entirely. Since the shutdown, she said, UNC has been reevaluating institutional and regulatory requirements to ensure the replacement meets current needs. Viera said the University hopes to have a minimum viable product available by the end of 2026, with plans to continue developing the platform afterward. The loss of Research For Me has created recruitment challenges for researchers who relied on the platform to connect with potential study participants. Muscatell said her lab was unable to recruit enough participants to meet the requirements of a study after the platform became inaccessible. She said her lab has explored alternatives, including social media advertisements, campus flyers and Craigslist. However, she noted these methods can be costly, lack credibility and offer more limited outreach than Research For Me. “To my knowledge, there aren’t a lot of other ways for people in the general public to identify research opportunities,” Muscatell said. Emani’ Davis, a former member of the UNC women’s volleyball team, participated in a monthslong research study with the whole team in 2024 examining how menstrual cycles affect athletic performance. articles.title: Cruise lines and their passengers spent $35 million in Maine last year
articles.desc: The new figures were collected through research done by the Maine Office of Tourism and Cruise Maine.
articles.content: Cruise lines and their passengers spent $35 million in Maine last year | Maine Public Scroll down to see all available streams. Cruise lines and their passengers spent $35 million in Maine last year Published November 16, 2026 at 1:02 PM EST More than 3,000 visitors at eight ports in Maine were surveyed regarding their experiences onshore, their likelihood to return to the state and the economic impact of their spending while cruising here in 2025. Cruise visitors and cruise lines, including crews, spent $35 million statewide. That provided $28 million to Maine's GDP, $3 million in tax revenue and supported 450 jobs. Most surveyed said Maine's ports were welcoming and service at restaurants was very good. Nearly 60% recommend Maine for its shore experiences and 40% said they would return. Each visitor spent about $80 during a port visit with 68% staying overnight before a cruise began, with an average expense of $140 per night. The average cruise visitor tends to be 60 or older and lives in the Northeast or Southeast. When Portland visitors are segregated from all other visitors: Cruise passengers and cruise lines spent a combined $22 million in the Portland area, out of the $35 million in cruise-related spending statewide. That spending increased Portland's gross domestic product by $17.5 million, out of $28 million statewide. Cruise-related economic activity also supported 300 full-time equivalent jobs in the Portland area, out of 450 statewide, and generated $1.8 million in state tax revenue, out of $3 million statewide. A Portland-based watchdog group said a survey of cruise visitors to Maine fails to paint a clear picture of the real impacts of the industry on the state. Portland Cruise Control said the data highlighted by the state office of tourism and industry supporters doesn't include effects on public health, infrastructure and the environment. It also questioned disembarkation rates that were provided by the Cruise Line International Association, which it said is a biased source. articles.title: Ubuntu gets AI-generated security fixes for those feeling brave
articles.desc: Opt-in Edge archive gives Pro subscribers early access before full testing, while normal updates remain human-validated
articles.content: Ubuntu gets AI-generated security fixes for those feeling brave Ubuntu gets AI-generated security fixes for those feeling brave Opt-in Edge archive gives Pro subscribers early access before full testing, while normal updates remain human-validated Japan's Fugaku supercomputer has decidedly un-super security US extends chip sale restrictions to more Asian countries to reduce risk of ‘diversion’ to China California sues OpenAI for misleading public about AI safety Infoblox customer and staff data exposed in Sharepoint breach Attackers are using AI agents to automate cybercrime at 'industrial scale,' FBI and AWS warn Canonical is offering Ubuntu Pro users an opt-in channel for AI-generated security patches, deploying bots to help tackle the growing pile of vulnerabilities other bots are uncovering. Canonical's VP for "Excellence Engineering," Pierre Guillemin, gave the second keynote at the recent Ubuntu Summit, introducing the , an optional repository of security fixes generated by the company's Surge framework. As the announcement describes it: "We built Surge, a multi-agent orchestration framework for CVE remediation and backporting, and have reached a high level of confidence in its capabilities. We will not automatically upload Surge-generated fixes to our stable releases, but from today they are available to Ubuntu Pro users in the new Edge archive." Edge offers patches before extended testing and qualification are complete, allowing users to assess them themselves. Canonical says updates delivered through the normal security channels will remain human-validated. Ubuntu Summit now runs twice a year. Last week's , the company announced a move into agentic AI, but this new one is bolder still. Guillemin noted that "October 2026 saw almost as many CVEs as all of 2025." Surge is a "multi-agent orchestration framework" to remediate vulnerabilities in Ubuntu's userspace. In other words, not the kernel, but even so, it is ambitious. The idea is to use a group of different LLMs to triage new vulnerabilities, find existing fixes, use multiple competing models to backport them to the versions in Ubuntu, and run automatic testing on them. Then a different group of "judging models" will evaluate the fixes and look for consensus. When candidates are chosen, they pass through normal Ubuntu package testing. If there are edge cases, low confidence scores, deadlocks, or other problems, then the process will be escalated to the staff of Canonical's security team. Ubuntu Summit 26.10 Thursday keynotes – Pierre Guillemin's begins at 27 minutes in. It's an attempt, as Guillemin put it, "to use AI to fight AI" – cooperating groups of LLMs patching their way through the ever-increasing flow of security holes. Even so, this is a remarkably courageous tactic (at the risk of using a It's an opt-in feature of Ubuntu Pro, Canonical's security and support subscription – although as we , Pro also has a free tier, so security researchers and the community can try Edge out, study it, and report their findings. We do sympathize with companies struggling against a rising tide of bot-powered security hole discovery. In theory, corporate funding can pay for faster fixes than a volunteer community can offer, but even for commercial vendors these are testing times. As we reported , surveys suggest that Ubuntu is about a third of the world Linux user base. Some of those users will be intrepid enough to try this, and that will end up being informative for the whole FOSS world. Those with long memories will remember the last time Canonical used the same edgy nomenclature.
